alt: Paper 2 Listening lasts about 35-45 minutes and is worth 30 marks, 33% of the qualification against Paper 1's 60 marks and 67%. Everything is heard twice. Practice relies on general Urdu listening material because exam audio is released only to centres.
caption: Half Paper 1's marks, but a full third of the grade.

alt: Paper 2's four exercises: 1 short answer questions on short texts (8 marks, L1 and L2), 2 gap-fill on one longer text (8 marks, L1 and L2), 3 multiple matching of six speakers (6 marks, L3 and L4), and 4 multiple-choice on a two-speaker discussion (8 marks, L1 to L4).
caption: Short texts first, a two-speaker discussion last.

alt: A grid of the four listening objectives against the four exercises: Exercises 1 and 2 test L1 and L2, Exercise 3 tests L3 and L4, and Exercise 4 tests all four, L1 to L4.
caption: Literal objectives early, inference later, everything in Exercise 4.

alt: A scale from stated facts to implied meaning. Exercises 1 and 2 test facts such as times, places and names; Exercise 3 asks you to tell speakers' views apart by tone and opinion words; Exercise 4 needs inference about sarcasm, hesitation and changes of mind.
caption: The paper moves from what is said towards what is meant.

alt: Every exercise is heard twice: use the first hearing for gist, rough location of answers and notes, and the second to fill in and check precise details before writing. Speaking practice for Component 5 overlaps with these listening skills.
caption: Gist and location first time, precise details second time.
